$comment: THE PROPOSAL'S content contract, and only the proposal's. Ghost deck test: reading only the titles in order must tell the full argument. Every title is a full declarative assertion, never a topic label. One evidence shape per slide. A DISCOVERY deck inverts the title rule and the item bound and keeps no structured copy of its content at all - SKILL.md step 5 says which rules go the other way, and discovery-deck.html beside it is the starting point. Validating a discovery deck against this schema goes green on a deck that has compressed the customer's document into something only its author can read.

audience.$comment: Who is in the room and what they are there to do: whoever decides, for a proposal; whoever will operate it, for a handover.

slides.$comment: Decks of 12+ slides need a chapter divider every 4-6 slides and at least one quote or metrics slide. Never more than 5 consecutive content slides.

eyebrow.$comment: Stable cross-slide section label. Must never restate the title in different words.

title.$comment: A page-unique declarative claim, e.g. 'Q3 revenue grew 23% because enterprise deals closed 2x faster'. It names what is on the page; it does not count it - SKILL.md step 1.

items.$comment: 3-5 supporting items; each fits one line. A slide with fewer than 3 items and no chart merges into a neighbor.

cap.$comment: Why this slide matters: a tradeoff, boundary, next step, or insight the visual cannot say. Never restates the title or the diagram. Optional and exceptional rather than a slot every slide fills - what may go in one, the test it has to pass, and how often a finished deck earns one at all are the .co entry in design.md beside this file.
